speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for those results; the elevated alkaline phosphatase and ultrasound findings of bile duct thickening strongly suggest an obstruction. Have you recently undergone any gallbladder or biliary surgery, or do you have any history of pancreatic issues?

speaker: Patient
text: 32-year-old male. The patient reports a 2-month history of increasing generalized fatigue and severe pruritus. He has known hypertension and was diagnosed with ulcerative colitis 5 years ago. He mentions being sexually active with 2 female partners and inconsistent condom use.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Primary Sclerosing Cholangitis (PSC).

Given your history of ulcerative colitis, the combination of severe itching, elevated alkaline phosphatase, and ultrasound showing bile duct thickening is highly characteristic of PSC. The ultrasound finding of "thickening" without a visible stone or mass helps rule out simple choledocholithiasis. Do you have any right upper quadrant pain or fever?
